**Verdict: mixed, leaning no**
Xi’s 2024 economy was more stable than crisis-ridden, but I do not see convincing evidence that it ended the year on a clearly stronger trajectory than it inherited. There were real stabilization measures and some growth held up, yet the medium-term picture still looked burdened by weak demand, property stress, debt overhang, and only partial rebalancing. This is an inference from the balance of sources, not a direct apples-to-apples comparison source.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Pro | National Economy was Generally Stable with Steady Progress in the First Half Year | National Bureau of Statistics of China | 2024-07-15 | https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202407/t20240715_1955620.html | Official H1 data said GDP grew 5.0%, employment and prices were generally stable, and incomes kept rising. That supports a claim of stabilization, though not necessarily a stronger long-run trajectory. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.6 |
| Pro | China’s finance ministry pushes broad-based growth agenda | Xinhua / english.www.gov.cn | 2024-03-25 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202403/25/content_WS6600afebc6d0868f4e8e569e.html | The ministry promised fair treatment for firms, more tax relief/procurement balance, and more spending on education, healthcare, social security, and environmental protection. That is evidence of a broader growth strategy. | 5B.10, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.7 |
| Pro | NDRC says it will keep helping private enterprises | Xinhua / english.news.cn | 2024-01-10 | https://english.news.cn/20240110/78198229d70d4ad2824f8b50c3bedeee/c.html | Beijing said it would keep helping private enterprises, protect entrepreneurs’ rights, and use private-sector feedback in macro policy. That is a real pro-growth signal rather than pure patronage. | 5B.10, 5B.4, 5B.6, 5B.7 |
| Pro | China unveils new property support measures amid concerns about Evergrande fallout | Reuters | 2024-01-31 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-unveils-new-property-support-measures-amid-concerns-about-evergrande-fallout-3287774 | Beijing cut downpayments and mortgage floors and used SOE purchases plus completion financing to stabilize households and developers. This was a real crisis response. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.6, 5B.7 |
| Pro | China orders indebted local governments to halt some infrastructure projects | Reuters | 2024-01-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/exclusivechina-orders-indebted-local-governments-to-halt-some-infrastructure-projectssources-3277972 | Beijing told heavily indebted local governments to delay or halt some unfinished infrastructure projects, a corrective move against overborrowing. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.6 |
| Pro | China bans exports of gallium, germanium, antimony to US as trade tensions escalate | Reuters | 2024-12-03 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/china-bans-exports-of-gallium-germanium-antimony-to-us-3750488 | China actively responded to external pressure with export restrictions on critical minerals, showing some capacity to manage sanctions-like constraints. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.4 |
| Con | IMF Staff Completes 2024 Article IV Mission to the People’s Republic of China | IMF | 2024-05-28 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/05/28/pr24184-china-imf-staff-completes-2024-art-iv-mission | The IMF said inflation was subdued, output was below potential, and more easing plus exchange-rate flexibility were still needed. That undercuts a claim that the economy was clearly on a stronger path already. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.7 |
| Con | IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation with the People’s Republic of China | IMF | 2024-08-02 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/31/pr24295-china-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult | The IMF said weak productivity, aging, debt, and property/local-government risks still dragged on the outlook and that a comprehensive reform package was needed. That is strong evidence against a durable stronger trajectory. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.7 |
| Con | People’s Republic of China: 2024 Article IV Consultation | IMF | 2024-08-02 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/08/01/peoples-republic-of-china-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-552803 | IMF said a neutral fiscal stance, stronger social safety nets, and debt consolidation were needed, and that fiscal, debt, and monetary frameworks still had weaknesses. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.7 |
| Con | China’s consumer prices suffer biggest fall since 2009 as deflation risks stalk economy | Reuters | 2024-02-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/chinas-consumer-prices-suffer-biggest-fall-since-2009-as-deflation-risks-stalk-economy-3296540 | Reuters reported the steepest consumer-price fall since 2009, showing that the demand problem was still severe early in the year. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3 |
| Con | China’s home de-stocking push to bring developers little cheer | Reuters | 2024-06-09 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/chinas-home-destocking-push-to-bring-developers-little-cheer-3476774 | The de-stocking program was too small to meaningfully revive cash-strapped developers, so the property correction remained partial. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.6 |
| Con | China unveils steps to tackle hidden debt of local governments | Reuters | 2024-11-08 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/china-unveils-steps-to-tackle-hidden-debt-of-local-governments-2347705/ | The debt swap improved transparency but also raised official debt and squeezed new project funding, which looks like stabilization after overborrowing rather than a clean upward reset. | 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.7 |
| Con | China passes law granting Communist Party more control over cabinet | Reuters | 2024-03-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-passes-law-granting-communist-party-more-control-over-cabinet-3331891 | Reuters said the revised State Council law increased Party control over the cabinet and removed some public accountability space, which weakens confidence in a rule-based long-run trajectory. | 5B.10, 5B.2, 5B.6, 5B.7 |

**Bottom line**
- Stronger than inherited: some evidence of stabilization, infrastructure triage, private-firm support, and targeted property/debt repairs.
- Not clearly stronger overall: IMF and Reuters still point to weak demand, deflation risk, debt overhang, and an insufficiently rebalanced model.
- Net: Xi appears to have stabilized the economy, not clearly improved its long-run trajectory.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single 2024 source that directly and cleanly compares “inherited economy vs. end-2024 economy” under one methodology.
- The conclusion is therefore an inference from 2024 outcome data, IMF assessments, and policy responses under external constraints.
